text.p: Investors should hold shares in Polish brewer Okocimskie Zaklady Piwowarskie SA (Okocim) after the stock's rise by about 67 percent this year, Salomon Brothers said in a report.
"We are initiating coverage of Okocim...with a Hold recommendation in the belief that the company's improved performance is already reflected in the share price," the report dated September 16 said.
Since then the stock has slipped to 21.1 from 21.5 zlotys.
Salomon said Okocim and Zywiec, the country's best-known brands, could face increasing competition from northern Polish Elbrewery SA and Poznan-based Lech Browary Wielkopolski SA.
All four Polish brewers have foreign strategic investors, with Carlsberg holding 32 percent of Okocim.

"As virtually all the largest beer producers have completed costly investment programmes to increase their capacities and distribution channels, gaining market share will prove difficult for even the best producers," Salomon said.
But it said a good sign was that beer consumption was expected to rise by seven to 10 percent annually to the end of the decade from the current 40 litres per person.
Salomon said Okocim's net income would grow 85 percent in 1996 and 35 percent in 1997. It said earnings per share should rise by 30 percent this year and five percent next year.
